subject.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands

question: Should non-yolo OpenClaw gateway/daemon lifecycle commands always bypass durable allowlist and auto-review paths in favor of explicit human approval, despite changing existing automation behavior?
rationale: The branch is a coherent implementation of the reported bug, but the deliberately fail-closed change affects existing operator workflows and the issue/PR evidence itself identifies maintainer confirmation of the security policy as separate from runtime proof.

options.title: Adopt explicit lifecycle approval
options.body: Confirm that non-yolo lifecycle mutations must require direct approval, then review the matcher’s scope and upgrade behavior as the permanent security contract.

options.title: Preserve current automation behavior
options.body: Do not change the default approval path until maintainers choose a narrower policy or an explicitly opt-in strict mode.

recommendation.title: Adopt explicit lifecycle approval
recommendation.body: Confirm that non-yolo lifecycle mutations must require direct approval, then review the matcher’s scope and upgrade behavior as the permanent security contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-level security and compatibility decision rather than a mechanical contributor-follow-up item.
